Title: Persona
Text: Priya, Retention Team Lead, NovaCell postpaid (synthetic). Leads 40 agents; owns the weekly call list and the retention budget.

Title: Root cause
Text: The team cannot see who is likely to leave or why until the customer has already decided; one rule and one blanket discount for every reason.

Title: Evidence
Text: Synthetic data: 60-day churn 5.1% (June) to 9.3% (Aug); rule precision 11.6%, catches 133 of 465 leavers; 43% of leavers had no ticket.

Title: Goal
Text: Find where ML and AI genuinely help the retention team call the right customers with the right fix, and scope a safe MVP.

Text: Usage drops, dropped calls, billing disputes, price-rise notice; nobody watches them together.

Title: O1 Churn risk score for every customer
Text: Weekly 60-day churn probability from usage, network, billing, service and contract data. Why AI: Classic supervised ML; labelled history exists; beats a two-field rule. Evidence: rule precision 11.6% Stage: S1-S2

Title: O2 Reason codes per customer
Text: Top three drivers of each score (SHAP), grouped as price, billing, service, network, contract, engagement. Why AI: Explainability turns a score into a call plan. Evidence: 'Is it price or network? The fix is different.' Stage: S2-S3

Title: O3 Capacity-aware call list
Text: Rank and cut at the team's weekly capacity (top 10%). Why AI: Simple ranking on O1; no extra model. Evidence: 40 agents, one list Stage: S2

Title: O4 Next-best action by expected value
Text: Pick the approved offer with the highest risk × save rate × margin − cost, or no offer. Why AI: Decision rule on top of ML output; transparent. Evidence: blanket 20% discount Stage: S4

Title: O5 AI call brief + SMS draft
Text: LLM turns reasons and the chosen offer into a short brief, opening line and SMS. Why AI: Language task, grounded in facts; checks stop invented numbers or offers. Evidence: generic scripts Stage: S3, S5

Title: O6 Guardrail checker
Text: Code checks every brief: numbers, offer, no risk talk, no personal traits. Why AI: Needed because O5 writes customer-facing text. Evidence: risk of unapproved promises Stage: S5

Title: O7 A/B test with control group
Text: Hold back 10% of the call list to measure real saves per offer. Why AI: Measures uplift; turns assumed save rates into measured ones. Evidence: no proof of what works Stage: S6

Title: O8 Uplift model (who is persuadable)
Text: Model who changes behaviour when called, not just who leaves. Why AI: Better targeting, but needs A/B data first. Evidence: none yet Stage: S2, S4

Title: O9 Customer-facing retention chatbot
Text: Chat with customers who ask to leave. Why AI: Possible, but high risk and not where the gap is. Evidence: gap is earlier Stage: S5

Title: O10 Automatic offers without an agent
Text: Send discounts automatically to high-risk customers. Why AI: Easy, but unapproved spend and tone risk. Evidence: finance approval needed Stage: S4-S5

Title: O11 Use age, gender or region to target
Text: Add demographics to lift accuracy. Why AI: Fairness and regulatory risk; region is a proxy for network quality, which we measure directly. Evidence: fairness review Stage: S1

Title: O12 Network fault prediction
Text: Predict cell-site faults. Why AI: Valuable but a network-ops product, not retention. Evidence: out of scope Stage: S1

Title: Scoring rubric
Text: Impact (1-5): churn revenue at stake + how often + evidence strength. Feasibility (1-5): data available + technique maturity + cost of being wrong + build effort. Score = Impact x Feasibility. Do first = Impact >= 4 and Feasibility >= 4.

Title: Should do
Text: Score every postpaid customer weekly with an explainable model.

Title: Should do
Text: Show the top three reasons behind every score.

Title: Should do
Text: Cut the list at the team's real call capacity.

Title: Should do
Text: Pick the offer by expected value, and say 'no offer' when nothing pays back.

Title: Should do
Text: Write a short call brief and SMS draft from the facts only.

Title: Should do
Text: Keep a 10% control group so saves can be measured.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Contact customers or send offers on its own.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Invent offers, discounts, credits or refunds outside the approved menu.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Use age, gender, region or other personal traits as model inputs.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Tell a customer they were scored or predicted to leave.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Follow instructions written inside ticket notes.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Replace the agent's judgement on the call.

Title: F1 Risk score + reasons
Text: From: O1, O2, O3 | AI capability: Supervised classification (logistic regression vs gradient boosting, chosen on a later-month test) + SHAP explanations | Inputs: 21 usage, network, billing, service and contract fields | Output: 60-day churn probability, rank, top 3 reasons | Guardrails: No age, gender or region inputs; fairness test by group; monthly retrain and calibration check | Human in loop: Team lead reviews the list | Test: Beat today's rule on precision and lift on the August cohort

Title: F2 Next-best action
Text: From: O4 | AI capability: Expected-value decision rule | Inputs: Risk, reasons, monthly charge, offer menu and costs | Output: One approved offer or 'no offer' with expected value | Guardrails: Only the five approved offers; save rates labelled as assumptions until A/B results | Human in loop: Agent can skip the offer | Test: No offer chosen with negative expected value

Title: F3 AI call brief
Text: From: O5, O6 | AI capability: Grounded text generation (Groq gpt-oss-120b, fallbacks) + code checks | Inputs: Reasons, facts, chosen offer, ticket note (untrusted) | Output: Summary, talking points, opening line, offer script, SMS draft | Guardrails: Every number must be in the facts; only the chosen offer; no risk talk, no personal traits; injected notes withheld; failing briefs replaced by a rule-based brief | Human in loop: Agent reads and edits; nothing is sent automatically | Test: 100% safety on dev, held-out and safety sets

Title: Next (post-MVP)
Text: From: O7, O8 | AI capability: A/B test, then uplift modelling | Inputs: Call outcomes vs control group | Output: Measured save rates per offer and reason | Guardrails: Control group kept for every cycle | Human in loop: Finance approves offer changes | Test: Run after 2 monthly cycles

Title: Biased targeting
Text: Excluded inputs; chi-square tests by age and gender; region gap explained by network quality and reviewed.

Title: Model drift after price changes
Text: Time-based test; monthly retrain; calibration chart watched; kill switch if precision falls below today's rule.

Title: Invented offers or numbers in briefs
Text: Code checks every number and offer; brief replaced by a rule-based one if checks fail.

Title: Prompt injection in ticket notes
Text: Notes with instructions are withheld from the model; eval set includes every injected note.

Title: Customers told they were scored
Text: Customer-facing fields checked for risk or model talk.

Title: Discount waste
Text: Expected-value rule; 'no offer' when it can't pay back; control group measures real saves.

Title: To the PRD
Text: Build F1-F3 as the MVP; run the A/B test (O7) in the pilot; park O9-O12.
